MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  MAY 16, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:04 p.m. at the George F Canyon Nature Center (deck
  area) at 27305 Palos Verdes Dr East, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274, by CHAIR
  CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  Romanelli, Retz (joined at 6:06 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF APRIL 18, 2022

  COMMISSIONER  PERSICHINA  made  a  motion,  seconded  by
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE MINUTES AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  RESCHEDULING OF PEPPERWOOD, ROCKBLUFF, AND SILVER SPUR

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
MAY 16, 2022
   PARK TOURS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER RETZ joined the meeting at 6:06 p.m.

  Based upon input from staff and Commissioners, the Commission concurred to hold
  the Pepperwood Park tour in September, cancel the Silver Spur Park tour and meet
  at Rockbluff Park in coordination with the ribbon cutting once new play equipment
  is installed.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  SUMMER EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview about the
  upcoming Mayor’s Ride and Summer movie and concert in the park events, adding
  that staff would reach out to youth acts to participate in the Concert in the Park
  program. ACM Davis noted that the Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament had been
  postponed to October. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the City Celebration event
  will take place in September. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed
  it would. ACM Davis also noted the PV Street Fair Pepper Tree Foundation booth
  is still in need of volunteers. COMMISSIONER POPE noted that school is almost
  out and getting kids to play for the summer concert may be difficult. She suggested
  reaching out to Amuse Music. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked about an
  upcoming City Celebration subcommittee meeting. Community Services Supervisor
  Pinuelas noted a meeting will take place in the near future and the subcommittee
  will be contacted.

  ACM Davis invited more Commissioners to join the Mayor’s Ride noting some
  equestrians may not be available to attend this year. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA asked if last year’s event had a good turnout. ACM Davis noted it
  had good attendance and that the food was well received even though the Scouts
  were not available last year. She added they were not available again this year.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that Rockbluff Park looked good.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the George F Canyon deck was missing
  railing on poles by station two. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the
  issue.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
MAY 16, 2022
   VICE CHAIR BAIN asked about Kids to Parks Day which she learned about at the
  prior City Council meeting. ACM Davis explained it was an awareness day to get
  kids out to play, the City posted a social media post and will use to promote the
  City’s park and recreation activities. She added that this was the third year the City
  promoted Kids to Parks Day and that an activity at the park could be included for
  next year’s campaign.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 26, 2022 SPECIAL MEETING

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 26, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE/TRAIL,
  DAPPLEGRAY PARK, TABER GROVE, AND BUTCHER PARK
  Ms. Holly Gray, Education Director of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy (PVPLC), gave an overview of the Nature Center’s Programs from
  the prior year.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if staff was furloughed during the shutdown. Ms.
  Gray stated PVPLC staff was furloughed during the shut down but staffing was
  reorganized to be better than it had been.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked how the Nature Center programs were
  advertised. Ms. Gray stated that they are advertised through the City’s E-
  newsletters and social media in addition to newspaper advertisements and the
  PVPLC’s social media account sharing that marketing depends on the event.

  ACM Davis provided the Commission an update regarding the New Nature Center
  re-build project. She shared that the City is working with the architect to consider
  changes for potential cost savings and operational attributes based on input from
  the PVPLC. She also shared that funding through grants and discretionary funds
  continue to be researched and applied for, adding that results regarding
  discretionary fund requests will be released in June. ACM Davis also shared that

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
MAY 16, 2022
   phase one of the Interpretive Design is being spearheaded by the PVPLC who is
  working with Acorn, the company who provided past work.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the size of the parking. ACM Davis
  that a CEQA analysis is concluding which will be open for public comment soon,
  but parking is being assessed to also include additional street side parking on Palos
  Verdes Drive East.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO DAPPLEGRAY PARK FOR
  A TOUR**

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith gave an overview of maintenance
  completed during the walkthrough of Dapplegray Park. He noted the footing of the
  arena and the six feet of crushed asphalt which provides drainage.

  ACM Davis gave a brief overview and update of the Butcher Park project. She
  shared details regarding the Metropolitan Water District’s (MWD) project which will
  delay the development of the project to Summer 2023, however plans and
  specifications with the landscape architect are being completed with the
  expectation to go out to bid in the Spring of 2023.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there was any assurance the MWD project would
  start as planned. ACM Davis noted that a contract agreement was secured for a
  ten-month project with penalty fees to be assessed if it takes longer.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there would be boulders placed in front
  of the park. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that is in the works. ACM
  Davis added that additional safety features will also be added using park facilities
  fees.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted weeding of the Taber Grove area
  due to recent rains.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the owner of the barn near Taber Grove
  could have it painted. ACM Davis noted staff will assess the encroaching items
  again and work with Community Development and Code Enforcement accordingly.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the ownership of the patch of land
  next to the encroachment. ACM Davis noted the City owns that land. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith noted the City was permitted to take down the pipe stalls
  in the area as it belonged to the City.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK to

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
MAY 16, 2022
   approve as follows:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 6:56 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JUNE 20, 2022, AT
  6:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK, 25851
  HAWTHORNE BLVD., ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
MAY 16, 2022
